definitions.explanation: The hereditary nobility created in the Meiji era from the former court nobles and feudal lords, later joined by statesmen and others honored for service. It was abolished under the postwar constitution in 1947.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{華族|かぞく}だった。
{華族|かぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{屋敷|やしき}→屋敷：12395_yashiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: A peer's mansion still stands today.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦後|せんご}→戦後：12853_sengo⟧、{華族|かぞく}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: After the war, the peerage system was abolished.

notes:
From 1884 the peers held five ranks: ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧ (prince or duke), {侯爵|こうしゃく} (marquis), ⟦{伯爵|はくしゃく}→伯爵：11721_hakushaku⟧ (count), {子爵|ししゃく} (viscount), and ⟦{男爵|だんしゃく}→男爵：13585_danshaku⟧ (baron). Peers sat in the House of Peers ({貴族院|きぞくいん}) of the prewar Diet.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {華族|かぞく}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧: the peerage system
- {華族|かぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{出|で}: of noble birth
- ⟦{元|もと}→元：03878_moto⟧{華族|かぞく}: a former peer

WATCH OUT:
- ⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧: family — the everyday word with the same reading; {華族|かぞく} appears only in historical contexts
